Assessment of BA.evidence_source: The BAS, which measures aspects of positive body image, is a 13-item scale that has been shown to have a unidimensional structure when completed by Western women (Avalos et al., 2005; Swami, Stieger, Haubner, & Voracek, 2008), with good test–retest reliability (Avalos et al., 2005) and good construct and discriminant validity (Avalos et al., 2005; Swami, Stieger, et al., 2008). All items were rated on a 5-point Likert-type scale (1 = Never, 5= Always) and responses on all 13 items were averaged to obtain an overall BAS score (higher scores reflected greater body appreciation). Cronbach's alpha for this scale was .90.

section_summary.extract_value: This section describes the measures used: the SATAQ-3 (30 items, four subscales) to assess media influences, reporting Cronbach's alphas for Information (.87), Pressure (.83), Internalisation-General (.91), and Internalisation-Athlete (.93); and the Body Appreciation Scale (BAS; 13 items) to measure positive body image (Cronbach's alpha = .90). No sample characteristics (country, N, age, ethnicity, education, BMI), survey administration method, or correlations between BAS and BMI are reported in this excerpt.
